claims.statement: A scalar distribution-based extension framework is lifted to high-dimensional matrix representations for neural losses/layers.

claims.statement: No bad minima proposition concerns equality of global minima and convex hull of global minimizers, not absence of suboptimal stationary/local points.
Lifting proof invokes normalized nonnegative weights, distinct eigenvalues and sign/domain conventions; practical approximation uses four eigenvectors and five power iterations.
Bounded-cardinality variant has boundary continuity caveat; singleton is not dual-LP feasible and has a separate proof with negative unique discrete minimum.
Table1 neural Lovasz improves scalar in8of10 comparisons, but is not uniformly best; deviations are across test graphs.
